verses.text: Then Job answered:
“I know that’s true. But how can a person be in the right before God?
If someone wanted to argue a case with him, they couldn’t answer him even once in a thousand times.
God is wise at heart and mighty in strength. Who’s ever dug in against him and come out ahead?
He moves mountains before they know what hit them. He flips them over in his anger.
He shakes the earth out of its place, and its pillars tremble.
He tells the sun to stay down, and it doesn’t rise. He seals up the stars.
He alone stretches out the heavens and walks on the waves of the sea.
He made the Bear, Orion, the Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.
He does great things we can’t figure out, more wonders than anyone can count.
Look, he goes right past me, and I don’t see him. He moves on, and I don’t even sense him.
Look, he snatches things away. Who can stop him? Who’ll ask him, ‘What are you doing?’
“God won’t pull back his anger. Even Rahab’s helpers bow down beneath him.
So how could I answer him? How could I find the words to argue my case with him?
Even if I were in the right, I wouldn’t answer back. I’d plead with my judge.
Even if I called and he answered, I still wouldn’t believe he’d listened to my voice.
He breaks me with a storm and piles wound upon wound for no reason.
He won’t let me catch my breath. He fills me with bitterness.
If it’s about strength, look how mighty he is! If it’s about justice, he says, ‘Who’s going to summon me?’
Even if I’m in the right, my own mouth will condemn me. Even if I’m blameless, it’ll make me out to be crooked.
I’m blameless. I don’t care about myself. I can’t stand my life.
“It all comes to the same thing. That’s why I say he destroys both the blameless and the wicked.
When a scourge kills suddenly, he mocks what innocent people are going through.
The earth is handed over to the wicked. He covers the eyes of its judges. If it isn’t him, then who is it?
“My days are faster than a runner now. They fly by without seeing anything good.
They’ve swept past like fast ships, like an eagle swooping on its prey.
If I think, ‘I’ll forget my complaint, wipe the sadness off my face, and cheer up,’
I’m still scared of all my sorrows. I know you won’t hold me innocent.
I’m going to be condemned anyway. Why wear myself out for nothing?
Even if I wash myself with snow and scrub my hands clean with lye,
you’ll still throw me into a ditch. Even my own clothes will be disgusted with me.
He isn’t human like I am, so I can’t answer him or take him to court.
There’s no one to settle things between us, no one who can lay a hand on both of us.
Let him take his rod away from me and stop terrifying me.
Then I’d speak without being afraid of him, because that fear isn’t who I am inside.”
